title: Bestvina–Savin contraction on a convex polyhedron complex (App C)
body_html:
Bestvina–Savin contraction on a convex polyhedron complex

A convex polyhedron complex is a convex closed subset $A \subseteq E$ of a Euclidean space with a regular CW structure such that each closed cell $\bar F$ is a convex polyhedron, and every compact subset of $E$ meets finitely many cells. The cellular convex hull $\mathrm{CCH}(S)$ of $S \subseteq A$ is the smallest convex subcomplex containing $S$.

PL skeletal collapse lemmas

Lemma 1. Let $f : D \to A$ be PL, $F$ a cell of $A$ with $\dim F > \dim D$. There is a PL $g : D \to A$ with $g(D) \subseteq (f(D) \setminus F) \cup \partial F$ and $g = f$ off $F$.
proof_html:
Pick $z \in F \setminus f(D)$ (non-empty by dimensionality); "radial" projection from $z$ to $\partial F$ gives a PL retraction $A \setminus \{z\} \to A$, hence $g := p \circ f$.

Lemma 2. Let $f : D \to A$ PL, $d = \dim D$. There is PL $g$ with $g(D) \subseteq \mathrm{sk}_d A$ and $g = f$ on $f^{-1}(\mathrm{sk}_d A)$.

Proof. Induct on the skeletal level $r$ such that $f(D) \subseteq \mathrm{sk}_r A$, applying Lemma 1 to each $r$-cell.

Main contraction theorem

Theorem. Fix $x_0 \in A^{(0)}$. There exists a cellular contraction $H : A \times [0, 1] \to A$ with:

  • $H(y, 0) = y$, $H(y, 1) = x_0$ for all $y \in A$;
  • $H(y, [0, 1]) \subseteq \mathrm{CCH}(\{y, x_0\})$ for all $y \in A$.

The second condition (containment in CCH) is the crucial refinement beyond mere homotopy; it gives the (C2) support property used in Contraction map c: C_d(A) → C_{d+1}(A) (Bestvina–Savin).

Proof. Construct $H_F$ for cells $F$ inductively on $\dim F$. For a 0-cell $y$, pick a PL path in $\mathrm{sk}_1 \mathrm{CCH}(\{y, x_0\})$. For an $i$-cell $E$: define $f$ on $\partial(\bar E \times [0, 1])$ via the previously built $H_F$'s; extend to a "cone" using a point $z_E \in E$ and $w_E \in \mathrm{CCH}(\bar E \cup \{x_0\})$; apply Lemma 2 to land in $\mathrm{sk}_{i+1} \mathrm{CCH}(\bar E \cup \{x_0\})$.

$N$-equivariant version

Proposition. If $N$ is a finite reflection group of $A$ fixing $x_0$, and for every Weyl chamber $C$ of $N$, $\bar C \cap A$ is a subcomplex of $A$, then $H$ can be taken to be $N$-equivariant.

Proof. Build $H_0$ on a fundamental chamber and extend by equivariance.

Chain incarnation

Corollary. There is a chain homotopy $c_i : C_i(A) \to C_{i+1}(A)$ between $\id$ and $(p_{x_0})_*$ with the same support property: if $c_i(\sigma) = \sum c(\sigma, \tau) \tau$ and $c(\sigma, \tau) \ne 0$, then $\tau \subseteq \mathrm{CCH}(\sigma \cup \{x_0\})$.

This is the $c$ used throughout Contraction map c: C_d(A) → C_{d+1}(A) (Bestvina–Savin) and consequently in Acyclicity of C_d(Φ, V)[φ_x] for vertices x.

Example. For Schneider–Stuhler-style polysimplicial $A$ this recovers the original BS proof at integer depth; for DeBacker $r$-facets it handles general depth $r$.
